title: Model Decision Lab
blurb: Choose the move that addresses the actual cause.
source: AWS Certified AI Practitioner (AIF-C01) exam guide · Domain 3
hint: Drag each situation onto the response it calls for. Some responses on the board are there to tempt you.

items.label: An assistant must answer from private policies that change every week and cite the current source.
items.why: RAG retrieves current private evidence at request time and supports citations. Trade-off: Fine-tuning can adapt behavior, but it is a poor mechanism for frequently changing facts.

items.label: Thousands of examples demonstrate a stable report style that the base model fails to reproduce consistently.
items.why: Fine-tuning is appropriate for recurring behavior demonstrated by a curated example set. Trade-off: Few-shot prompting should still be tried first when it meets quality requirements at lower complexity.

items.label: A capable model must extract five fields into a validated JSON object; no new knowledge is required.
items.why: Clear instructions, examples, a schema, and validation address formatting without changing model weights. Trade-off: Fine-tuning becomes reasonable only if prompt-based extraction repeatedly fails at the required scale and quality.

items.label: A model must internalize specialized terminology from a very large unlabeled scientific corpus.
items.why: Continued pretraining adapts the model's language representations using large quantities of domain text. Trade-off: RAG remains preferable when the need is access to changing facts rather than deeper domain-language adaptation.

items.label: The system must inspect an order, request approval, call a refund API, and report the result.
items.why: A tool-using agent can orchestrate steps, but each tool needs narrow permissions, validation, and approval gates. Trade-off: A deterministic workflow is safer when the sequence is fixed and does not require model-directed planning.

items.label: A claims system must reason over a damage photograph together with the written incident description.
items.why: A multimodal model can jointly interpret visual and textual inputs. Trade-off: Separate specialist vision and text models may win when independent outputs, control, or lower cost matter more.

items.label: Ten million short records must be classified nightly under a tight budget after labels are available.
items.why: A smaller evaluated classifier can deliver adequate quality with much lower batch-inference cost. Trade-off: A foundation model may accelerate prototyping or create labels, but should earn its production cost through measured quality.

items.label: Published rules completely determine eligibility and every decision must be reproducible and auditable.
items.why: Exact, complete rules should be implemented directly rather than approximated by a probabilistic model. Trade-off: AI can assist document intake or explanation without owning the authoritative decision.
